shortMeaning: The first and best portion or beginning of something, often signifying priority, chief status, or the firstfruits offered to God.

definitionAndDerivation.rootWords: The Hebrew word רֵאשִׁית (rêʼshîyth) derives from the root רֹאשׁ (rôʼsh), meaning 'head' or 'chief.' This root conveys ideas of beginning, leadership, and prominence, which informs the meaning of רֵאשִׁית as the foremost or principal part of something.
definitionAndDerivation.literalMeaning: Literally, רֵאשִׁית denotes the start or first portion of a sequence, whether in time, place, or rank. It concretely refers to the 'beginning' of an event or entity, the 'chief' or most important part, or the 'firstfruits' of a harvest or offering.
definitionAndDerivation.kjvTranslationSummary: The KJV translates רֵאשִׁית primarily as 'the firstfruits' (4 times) and 'the chief' (4 times), with notable renderings including 'In the beginning' (3 times) and 'The first' (2 times), reflecting its varied use to indicate priority in time, rank, or value.

biblicalAndFigurativeUses.category: The Beginning of Time and Creation
biblicalAndFigurativeUses.explanation: This category encompasses the use of רֵאשִׁית to denote the absolute beginning of creation or significant periods, emphasizing God’s role as the initiator of all things. It highlights the foundational nature of beginnings in divine acts and historical events.

verses.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah came this word from the LORD, saying,
In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah came this word unto Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,
The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet against Elam in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying,

biblicalAndFigurativeUses.explanation: Here, רֵאשִׁית refers to the first portion of agricultural produce or dough that is consecrated and offered to God as an expression of gratitude and recognition of His provision. This use underscores the principle of giving God the best and first part of one’s blessings.

verses.text: The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the LORD thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk.
The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring unto the house of the LORD thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk.
As for the oblation of the firstfruits, ye shall offer them unto the LORD: but they shall not be burnt on the altar for a sweet savour. be burnt: Heb. ascend

Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye be come into the land which I give unto you, and shall reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest: sheaf: or, handful: Heb. omer
Of the first of your dough ye shall give unto the LORD an heave offering in your generations.
All the best of the oil, and all the best of the wine, and of the wheat, the firstfruits of them which they shall offer unto the LORD, them have I given thee. best: Heb. fat
The firstfruit also of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the first of the fleece of thy sheep, shalt thou give him.

That thou shalt take of the first of all the fruit of the earth, which thou shalt bring of thy land that the LORD thy God giveth thee, and shalt put it in a basket, and shalt go unto the place which the LORD thy God shall choose to place his name there.

And that we should bring the firstfruits of our dough, and our offerings, and the fruit of all manner of trees, of wine and of oil, unto the priests, to the chambers of the house of our God; and the tithes of our ground unto the Levites, that the same Levites might have the tithes in all the cities of our tillage.

And at that time were some appointed over the chambers for the treasures, for the offerings, for the firstfruits, and for the tithes, to gather into them out of the fields of the cities the portions of the law for the priests and Levites: for Judah rejoiced for the priests and for the Levites that waited. of the law: that is, appointed by the law for Judah: Heb. for the joy of Judah waited: Heb. stood

For in mine holy mountain, in the mountain of the height of Israel, saith the Lord GOD, there shall all the house of Israel, all of them in the land, serve me: there will I accept them, and there will I require your offerings, and the firstfruits of your oblations, with all your holy things. firstfruits: or, chief

And the first of all the firstfruits of all things, and every oblation of all, of every sort of your oblations, shall be the priest's: ye shall also give unto the priest the first of your dough, that he may cause the blessing to rest in thine house. And the first: or, And the chief
And they shall not sell of it, neither exchange, nor alienate the firstfruits of the land: for it is holy unto the LORD.

biblicalAndFigurativeUses.category: Chief, Principal, or Foremost in Rank or Quality
biblicalAndFigurativeUses.explanation: In this sense, רֵאשִׁית is used to describe the chief or best part of something, including leaders, strength, or choice items. It conveys the idea of superiority or preeminence within a group or context.

verses.text: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar. Babel: Gr. Babylon

Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel my people?
But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the LORD thy God in Gilgal.
And smote all the firstborn in Egypt; the chief of their strength in the tabernacles of Ham:
He smote also all the firstborn in their land, the chief of all their strength.
Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might.

He shall enter also into the glorious land, and many countries shall be overthrown: but these shall escape out of his hand, even Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon. glorious: or, goodly, etc.: Heb. land of delight, or, ornament
That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph. wine: or, in bowls of wine affliction: Heb. breach

biblicalAndFigurativeUses.category: The Beginning or Principal Element of Abstract Concepts
biblicalAndFigurativeUses.explanation: This category includes uses of רֵאשִׁית to indicate the starting point or chief aspect of intangible things such as wisdom, knowledge, sin, strife, or life’s stages. It reveals the word’s flexibility in expressing the foundational or initiating phase of various phenomena.

verses.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction. the beginning: or, the principal part
Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.
The LORD possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.
The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with.

O thou inhabitant of Lachish, bind the chariot to the swift beast: she is the beginning of the sin to the daughter of Zion: for the transgressions of Israel were found in thee. inhabitant: Heb. inhabitress
Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.
Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure:

biblicalAndFigurativeUses.category: Firstborn and Primacy in Family or Nation
biblicalAndFigurativeUses.explanation: Here, רֵאשִׁית relates to firstborn status or the primacy of a nation or people, emphasizing the honor, responsibility, and strength associated with being first. This use reflects cultural and theological significance tied to birth order and national identity.

verses.text: But he shall acknowledge the son of the hated for the firstborn, by giving him a double portion of all that he hath: for he is the beginning of his strength; the right of the firstborn is his. that: Heb. that is found with him
And smote all the firstborn in Egypt; the chief of their strength in the tabernacles of Ham:
He smote also all the firstborn in their land, the chief of all their strength.

And when he looked on Amalek, he took up his parable, and said, Amalek was the first of the nations; but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever. the nations: the nations that warred against Israel that: or, even to destruction
Israel was holiness unto the LORD, and the firstfruits of his increase: all that devour him shall offend; evil shall come upon them, saith the LORD.

closingReflection: Consider how the concept of רֵאשִׁית invites believers to recognize God's sovereign role as the initiator and chief over all things, and to offer Him the first and best of their lives and possessions. Reflect on how embracing this principle might shape your understanding of priority and devotion in your own faith journey.
